- When sentiment is negative (avg < 0) over recent days, model tends to overcorrect upward — reduce forecast peak values.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 73.0), model often overshoots and fails to cap — cap forecast at +5% above prior peak or adjust downward by 1–2 points if sentiment turns neutral or negative.
- If sentiment shows strong bullish momentum (avg > 0.3) but forecast is flat or declining, model underreacts — increase forecast by 0.5–1.5 points to match sentiment trend.
- Model consistently underestimates true price in early 30d horizon when sentiment is neutral or mildly bullish — add 0.5–1.0 to forecast for first 5–7 days if sentiment > 0.1.
- When sentiment is volatile (±0.3 or more), model overfits short-term noise — smooth forecast by averaging last 3–5 values or apply exponential decay filter.
- If true outcome exceeds forecast by >2.5% for 3+ consecutive days, model is lagging — adjust forecast upward by 0.5–1.0 per day until trend stabilizes.
- Model often overpredicts in 30d horizon when sentiment is weak (avg < 0.1) — reduce forecast by 0.5–1.0 if sentiment < 0.05 for 3+ days.
- Forecast tends to lag true price by 1–3 days when sentiment is bullish — add 0.5–1.0 to forecast for next 2–3 days if sentiment > 0.2 and price is rising.
